structures.name: testis
structures.definition: Oval gland in the scrotum, one on each side.
structures.why: It sits outside the body because sperm production needs a temperature about 2–3 °C below body temperature.

notes.nursing: Sudden severe scrotal pain is testicular torsion until proven otherwise: surgery within 6 hours saves it.
notes.medicine: Drains to the para-aortic lymph nodes because it develops near the kidneys and descends.

structures.name: epididymis
structures.definition: Coiled tube on the back of each testis.
structures.function: Stores sperm and lets it mature and gain the ability to swim.
structures.why: Sperm leaving the testis can’t yet swim; maturing here takes about two weeks.

notes.medicine: Epididymitis causes pain that eases when the testis is lifted, unlike torsion.

structures.name: vas deferens
structures.definition: Muscular tube carrying sperm from the epididymis up through the inguinal canal into the pelvis.
structures.function: Moves sperm toward the urethra during ejaculation.
structures.why: Its thick muscular wall propels sperm quickly when needed.

notes.medicine: Cut and tied in a vasectomy.

structures.name: seminal vesicle
structures.definition: Coiled gland behind the bladder, one on each side.
structures.function: Produces most of the seminal fluid, rich in fructose.
structures.why: The fluid gives sperm energy and volume to travel.

notes.medicine: Its duct joins the vas deferens to form the ejaculatory duct.

structures.name: prostate
structures.definition: Walnut-sized gland below the bladder, surrounding the first part of the urethra.
structures.function: Adds an alkaline fluid to semen.
structures.why: The fluid protects sperm from vaginal acidity.

notes.nursing: An enlarged gland causes poor stream, frequency and retention; a catheter may be needed.
notes.medicine: Felt on rectal examination; cancer usually starts in the peripheral zone.

structures.name: corpus cavernosum
structures.definition: Paired column of spongy erectile tissue along the upper part of the penis.
structures.function: Fills with blood to produce an erection.
structures.why: Trapping blood under pressure makes the organ rigid.

notes.medicine: Priapism (erection lasting over 4 hours) is a urological emergency.

structures.name: corpus spongiosum
structures.definition: Single column of erectile tissue on the underside of the penis, surrounding the urethra and expanding into the glans.
structures.function: Keeps the urethra open during erection.
structures.why: Softer than the paired columns, it doesn’t squeeze the urethra closed.

notes.nursing: During male catheterisation, hold the shaft upright to straighten the urethra through it.
